faq: Is Velo the same as the Wix CLI?
No. Velo is Wix's built-in development platform for sites, with backend files and collections. The CLI is for building apps. We work with both and tell you which fits your project.
Can you add backend code to my existing site?
Yes. We enable Velo on your site, or on a copy first if you prefer, and add the code there. Your pages and content stay as they are.
How do you keep API keys safe?
We store them in the Wix Secrets Manager and read them only in backend code, never in the browser. We never ask for passwords. Add us as a collaborator or send keys through a secure channel.
Will it handle lots of data?
We design for it. Wix collections have limits on size and request rates, so we use paging, indexes and background jobs. We tell you in the notes where the limits are.
desc:
Wix Velo backend code and APIs power the part of your app or site that visitors never see. Ecom Swift LLC writes data collections, backend functions, endpoints and scheduled jobs, with secrets stored safely and every endpoint tested.

## What is Wix Velo backend code?

Wix Velo backend code is server-side code that runs on Wix rather than in the visitor's browser. It stores and reads records in data collections, exposes web methods, answers HTTP function calls from outside, runs scheduled jobs and talks to other services. It can be written in Velo for a site or in the server code of a Wix app built with the Wix CLI.

## Why the backend decides how reliable everything feels

The pages and widgets are the visible part, but the backend decides whether they work. If a collection is open to the wrong users, private data leaks. If an endpoint trusts what the browser sends, anyone can send bad data. If a scheduled job fails silently, reports stop arriving and nobody knows why.

Backend errors are expensive because they are invisible until a customer complains. Writing the code carefully at the start, with checks and logging, makes problems visible and small.

## How backend quality affects your project

Good backend code makes the front end simpler and faster. Pages ask for exactly the data they need, and the server does the heavy work. Permissions protect records so each person only sees what they should. Secrets stay on the server instead of in code a visitor could read.

It also makes growth less painful. A clear collection structure and documented endpoints let another developer extend the project without guessing. How much data a site can handle depends on the platform and the way the queries are written, and we design with that in mind rather than promise a fixed limit.

## What solid backend work includes

- Data collections with fields, types and permissions set deliberately.
- Backend web methods for actions the page should trigger.
- HTTP functions for public endpoints that outside tools can call.
- Scheduled jobs for recurring tasks such as cleanups or reports.
- Calls to outside APIs, with timeouts and error handling.
- Keys and tokens stored in Wix Secrets Manager.
- Input checks on every value that arrives from outside.
- Handling for Wix events when something changes on the site.
- Logging that records failures with enough detail to diagnose them.
- Test cases and short documentation for each endpoint.

## How we write and test it

We begin by listing what the front end needs and what other systems must reach. From that we design the collections and the functions, then build them in your project. We test each function with normal input and with bad input, and we check that permissions block what they should.

The Basic package delivers one collection with permissions, a few backend functions, input checks and usage notes. Standard widens this to several collections, more functions, a public HTTP function, a scheduled job and Secrets Manager setup. Premium delivers a complete backend with event hooks, two outside API connections, test cases for every endpoint and an API reference document.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Describe who should be allowed to read and write each collection.
- Send sample data so we can test with realistic records.
- Keep API keys out of messages and move them into Secrets Manager.
- Keep the documentation up to date when the code changes.

**Avoid:**
- Putting secret keys in page code.
- Trusting values sent from the browser without checking them.
- Giving every collection public read and write access.
- Running long tasks inside a single request instead of a scheduled job.

## Who this is for

A site owner with a Velo front end that needs reliable server code. An app developer who prefers to focus on the interface. A business that needs a Wix site to exchange data with an outside system.

## What we need from you

A description of the data and actions you need, access to the site or app as a collaborator and sample records if you have them. We never need your password. If outside services are involved, send their documentation and test credentials through a safe channel.

Note that Velo and the Wix CLI are different tools. We will use whichever fits your project and tell you why.
